_meta.rendered_by_build:
build.py m3_proof() (edited 2026-10-10 15:23 by the build owner) renders, in array order: every logos[] entry as
  • ; awards[] then awards_withheld[] entries whose withheld_reason does not contain 'never promote' (h4 = title, caption = issuer, no image), so ELMA renders and the EV-201 item does not; partner_text[] then partner_text_site_only[] (partner + relationship) under the template's 'Partnerships' heading. logos_government[], site_mentions_not_partnerships[], site_copy, news, stats, testimonials_ref and not_proof are never read by the build.
_meta.order: Arrays are in recommended display order, strongest first.
_meta.schema_note: Site wording sits in site_* fields (site_title, site_date, site_issuer, site_image_copy) so the build cannot pick it up; the rendered fields are title/issuer (awards) and relationship (partners).
_meta.logo_treatment: logos[] (the wall, 29): single-colour white marks on transparency. logos_government[] (3, off the wall): the UAE state-emblem lockups (MOHRE, MoI/Dubai Civil Defence, Cabinet Affairs) as colour marks as published with the page-white removed, so no emblem is recoloured (white versions kept as alt_files.white_mark). All trimmed to the alpha > 0 bounding box, max 240x96 px, lossless WebP. display_css is an optical-size suggestion (CSS px); the template currently ignores it and fits each logo in a 139x40 slot at 1440 px.
_meta.legibility_fields: mono_legible = every text line in the mark reads at 1x in the build's 139x40 slot (the field name is kept from v1 and applies to the colour files too); identity_legible_1x = the name or mark that identifies the organisation reads; legibility.display_css_legible = the size at which the smallest line would read.
_meta.visible_caption: As published on meerana.ae (retrieved 2 October 2026). (build.py's own caption)
